newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat on first public visit to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat on first public visit to Israel.

text.p: A beaming Palestinian President Yasser Arafat paid his first public visit to Israel on Tuesday for talks with Israeli President Ezer Weizman in a further sign of an easing of Israel-PLO tensions.
An Israeli air force helicopter ferried the former guerrilla chief from the Gaza Strip to Weizman's private residence in the seaside town of Caesarea in central Israel.

The Palestinian leader's only previous visit to Israel -- at night and without advance announcement -- was a condolence call on the widow of assassinated prime minister Yitzhak Rabin last November in Tel Aviv.

Arafat's visit was another indication Israel and the PLO had pulled back from the brink after clashes last month, touched off by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem, killed 59 Palestinians and 15 Jews.

Weizman greeted Arafat, who was wearing his trademark khaki uniform and chequered keffiyeh, at the entrance to his whitewashed villa in Caesarea, a seafront community that boasts Israel's only golf course.

Arafat's wide smiles were in stark contrast to the gloomy image he projected in appearances before the media during an emergency White House summit last week with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Weizman, whose post is largely ceremonial, is viewed by many Arabs as a peacemaker. The former defence minister was an architect of the 1979 Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty.
Two months ago, Weizman embarrassed Netanyahu by saying he would meet Arafat if the right-wing prime minister continued to flinch from holding a summit with the Palestinian president.
Netanyahu has since met Arafat once in Gaza and again in Washington.
"We welcome any effort or contribution that can advance the peace process and Israel's interests in it," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said about Weizman's invitation to Arafat to come to his home.

Naveh told Israel Radio he expected Weizman's talks with Arafat would touch upon the current Israeli-PLO negotiations on how to implement Israel's long-delayed troop redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron.
Weizman has met Arafat twice, in 1994 at the inauguration of South African President Nelson Mandela and last January at the funeral of French President Francois Mitterrand.

By hosting Arafat at his private residence, rather than at his official office in Jerusalem, Weizman avoided the political uproar that a visit by the Palestinian leader to the holy city would have triggered among Israelis.
Arafat was due to spend several hours at Weizman's home before returning to Gaza.
